subject: Tenant segmentation & storage encryption for NovaPay on-prem deployment
messages:
From: Jordan Hsu <jordan.hsu@novapay.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-eng@novapay.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant isolation / encryption questions before kickoff

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the call today. Before we schedule the on-prem kickoff with our infra team, a couple of clarification items came up from our SREs: 

- We need confirmation on strong tenant isolation between our production and test workloads (node pool and namespace strategies).
- For data at rest, we must support FIPS-compatible LUKS encryption at node level, and ideally REK-like KMS integration for our HSM vault (we use AetherKMS).
- Can Redwood provide a recommended PV class mapping (fast/ssd for model caches, cold/hdd for logs) and the eviction behaviour under disk pressure?

Attaching a short list of regulatory constraints for reference (will follow with a separate secure transfer for the SOC artifacts).

Appreciate a one-page summary we can circulate to our legal and infra teams.

Jordan
SRE Lead, NovaPay
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hsu <jordan.hsu@novapay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation / encryption questions before kickoff

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers so we can get the kickoff scheduled; I put a compact runbook and node plan in the attached PDF (novapay-nodeplan-v1.pdf) and a PV mapping spreadsheet (pv-class-and-encryption-map.xlsx). Quick summary below: 

1) Tenant isolation: recommended pattern is separate node pools per tenant class (prod, staging, batch) + namespace admission controls. We suggest the following labels and taints:
   - prod-pool: taint redwood.k8s/role=prod:NoSchedule (GPU-backed cache pools if you're using model-serving on nodes)
   - staging-pool: lower-cost CPU nodes, no privileged PV mounts
   - batch-pool: burstable nodes with preemptible policy for nightly workloads

   Namespaces will be enforced with NetworkPolicy + PSP-like PodSecurity admission. We can provide the YAML for NetworkPolicy templates during kickoff.

2) Encryption at rest: Redwood supports LUKS device encryption at the OS/disk layer. For KMS integration we have a connector pattern to your AetherKMS — we do not store keys; customer-managed keys are used to provision node-level LUKS keys. For FIPS compatibility, we'll validate kernel crypto modules and send our verification checklist.

3) PV mapping & eviction: see spreadsheet for class names. Quick mapping: 
   - redwood-ssd-fast (local NVMe, high IOPS) -> model KV caches, ephemeral checkpointing
   - redwood-ssd-standard (networked NVMe/SSD) -> runtime state, small model layers
   - redwood-hdd-cold (SATA) -> logs, historical records

   Eviction policy: we recommend kubelet eviction thresholds of 5% free disk for prod-pool with a grace period and an LRU cache eviction sidecar for cache directories. We call out required monitoring alerts if free disk drops below 15%.

Next steps: Laura and Kimberly are looping in detailed sizing and compliance notes. Laura — can you add node counts for the initial POC and an ops checklist for bootstrapping encrypted nodes?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Hsu <jordan.hsu@novapay.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 13:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation / encryption questions before kickoff

Aditya / Jordan —

I took a quick pass at the initial sizing for the POC (30 days) and the initial 3-node profile we recommend is below (details in novapay-nodeplan-v1.pdf):

- prod-pool: 3 x mGPU-48 (48GB) nodes, NVMe local SSD (for KV caches), 8 vCPUs for sidecars, 512GB disk each
- staging-pool: 2 x cpu-16 nodes, standard SSD, 256GB disk each
- batch-pool: 2 x cpu-8 preemptible nodes, 1TB HDD for retained artifacts

Storage classes and encryption steps:
- During node bootstrap we will run a small agent to provision LUKS on the designated block devices and register the PV backend. Agent will call your AetherKMS via a customer-provided service principal.
- We tested LUKS + kubelet mounts in our internal lab; attaching results in pv-class-and-encryption-map.xlsx (sheet: "benchmarks").

Action items for NovaPay before kickoff:
1. Provide a service principal for AetherKMS with limited scope (key create/unwrap).
2. Confirm expected steady-state QPS for model-serving endpoints (helps decide NVMe sizing).
3. Share any internal hardening baseline (CIS, STIG) we should align with.

Kimberly — can you add the Kubernetes admission policy checklist and a short note on audit log retention?

-laura
Laura Bennett
Manager, On-Prem Deployments, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hsu <jordan.hsu@novapay.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation / encryption questions before kickoff

Jordan — quick note to close the loop prior to kickoff: 

- Audit logs: we recommend forwarding kube-audit to your SIEM with a 90-day warm retention and a 1-year cold archive; we'll provide the FluentD/Vector config.
- Admission controls: attached sample OPA Gatekeeper constraints for namespace quotas and disallowed hostPath mounts (I included them in Drive link).
- Eviction & monitoring: set nodefs.available threshold at 10% for non-prod and 5% for prod; configure Prometheus alerts to page on sustained drop > 3m.

I'll upload the admission policy templates and the FluentD config to the Drive link and share in HubSpot. Kickoff slot: Thursday 2028-06-21 10:00 PT — does that work for NovaPay?

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs: novapay-nodeplan-v1.pdf (18 pages), pv-class-and-encryption-map.xlsx (3 sheets)
